title: Chir Pine: Ancient Chir Pines You Can Visit
meta_description: A Himalayan resin pine with needles up to 30cm. In Rome one grows above Nero's buried Domus Aurea, from a seed a Tibetologist carried home.
intro: The chir pine belongs to the dry outer foothills of the Himalaya, the resin belt running from Pakistan through northern India into Nepal, where it is tapped for turpentine the way other trees are tapped for rubber. Its needles run up to thirty centimetres in bundles of three and hang rather than bristle, so a mature crown looks like a loose green waterfall rather than the stiff cone most people picture at the word pine. Every old one here is a long way from that range. Rome's monumental register lists exactly two, one of them on Colle Oppio, grown from a seed the Tibetologist Giuseppe Tucci carried back from an expedition and planted directly above Nero's buried Domus Aurea. Caserta's, about 150 years old, grows in the English Garden of a Bourbon palace, and Hobart's in the Royal Tasmanian Botanical Gardens' pinetum.
